candidates.statement: Now, in order for the gauge theory $T[M]$ to flow (in a straightforward way) to a superconformal theory in the infrared, two conditions are necessary: 1) some $U(1)_R$ R-symmetry must be preserved; and 2) there must exist a choice of $U(1)_R$ symmetry such that the charges of all chiral operators are non-negative, because in a superconformal theory R-charges are proportional to operator dimensions.

This means that we must be able to choose $\rho_i,\rho_i',\rho_i''$ for individual tetrahedra in such a way that the sums of these charges around any internal edge $E$ is 2, and all these charges are non-negative.

From this perspective, at least some of the BPS operators in $T[M]$ should come from M2 branes that end on the stack of M5 branes, such that their boundary $\pd$(M2)$=\Sigma\times\{0\} \subset M\times \BR^3$ wraps a surface in $M$.
